# Download and consume a merchant object from Node

The existing Node `Buyer` selects an original merchant object description,
retains one native whole-file or chunked acquisition, continues its untouched requests, assembles the
verified bytes, and passes the file to application code. Its native session also
opens in the original [object CLI](../OBJECTS.md), browser workspace and Python
application.

Use the same installed import and complete native runtime as the
[Node buyer guide](README.md):

```js
import { Buyer, ObjectDownloadError } from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/buyer/node';
// Standalone local companion package: '@stellar-forge/native-buyer'.

const buyer = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory: '/installed/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  stateDirectory: '/private/customer/purchases',
  timeoutMs: 900000, // Includes original terminal prompts and remaining requests.
});
```

The runtime includes `python/object-bridge.mjs`. This is JavaScript: Node calls
that released application directly; the bridge requires no Python interpreter.
The original SF36 operator separately uses its documented Python setup. Keep
the companion and native runtime at the same current distribution.

## Select and retain a download

Obtain the merchant's original `objects.json`, choose its `whole` or `chunks`
product, and prepare the corresponding original buyer configuration or operator
workspace. The initial operation is its base `GET` route without query, body or
response destination. The original engine retains a whole file as one query-free
request or derives each chunk's exact `offset` and `length`; both modes retain
their matching native inbox jobs.

```js
const acquisition = await buyer.createObject({
  id: 'archive-october',
  workspaceDirectory: '/private/operator/archive',
  descriptionFile: '/private/customer/merchant-objects.json',
  objectId: 'archive',
  maxTotalAtomic: '3000',
  chunkBytes: 921600, // Optional smaller size within the advertised chunk cap.
});
console.log(acquisition.lastReport.native);
```

These paths, alias and amounts are illustrative: select the actual merchant's
descriptor, reviewed terms and authorized spending limits. `id` is the customer's
stable application name, separate from the original session UUID and per-request
intent IDs. Preparation is offline.

The descriptor supplies route, byte count, snapshot, content type, chunk cap and
optional whole-file SHA-256. The application retains its exact bytes and selected
alias; the original selector validates them. `maxTotalAtomic` is an integer
string for the entire download and must cover
`ceil(bytes / chunkBytes) × per-request maxAtomic`. A 1,843,229-byte object in
921,600-byte chunks needs three requests; a 1,000-unit per-request ceiling needs
at least `"3000"` total allocation. These are ceilings. Original outcomes and
ledger entries remain the authority for the actual payment state. For a `whole`
descriptor, omit `chunkBytes`: the original engine fixes one request covering the
complete file, and the total allocation must cover one per-request ceiling.
An empty whole file still has one reviewed request and its original payment terms.

```js
const whole = await buyer.createObject({
  id: 'monthly-report',
  workspaceDirectory: '/private/operator/report',
  descriptionFile: '/private/customer/merchant-objects.json',
  objectId: 'report', // Select the actual merchant's whole-file alias.
  maxTotalAtomic: '1000',
});
console.log(whole.lastReport.native.deliveryMode); // 'whole'
const report = await whole.download('/private/customer/files/report.pdf');
await report.verify();
```

The original whole-file engine requires HTTP 200 without a range response,
checks the selected complete length, snapshot and digest, and keeps that one
intent for accounting and restart. The same `ObjectDelivery` supports a valid
zero-byte whole file; an empty chunked product remains invalid. Its verified
empty byte stream yields no chunks, while `verify()` and `saveAs()` still check
the original receipt and empty-file SHA-256. New Node bindings retain the native
delivery mode. Historical bindings without that field continue as chunks and
cannot silently change into a whole-file session.

Use `config: '/private/buyer.json'` or a JSON configuration object for an explicit
original operator configuration. `operatorProfile` can fill its original fields.
Supplying both config and workspace makes the native engine enforce their shared
operator/terms binding. A workspace-only call retains its saved configuration
and ignores the Buyer's global profile; a per-call profile requires config.

For an explicit byte contract, supply `bytes`, `chunkBytes`, `expectedSnapshot`,
and optionally `expectedSha256` and `expectedContentType`, without
`descriptionFile` or `objectId`. This explicit byte plan describes a positive-size
chunked product. Whole-file and empty-file selection use the original merchant
descriptor in the same named `ObjectAcquisition` workflow above.

## Return an application file

Run acquisition from the operator terminal. The original queue, approval and
spending policy remain in charge of each actual request.

```js
const controller = new AbortController();
const download = await acquisition.download('/private/customer/files/archive.zip', {
  signal: controller.signal,
});
console.log(download.path);
console.log(download.assembly); // Original snapshot, chunk-manifest hash and receipt.

for await (const chunk of download.chunks()) {
  // Feed the bytes to this application's temporary import/output destination.
}
// Commit that consumer's result only after iteration completes successfully.
await download.saveAs('/private/customer/export/archive-copy.zip');
```

Create the output parent as a private, caller-owned directory first. The original
command checks a new location before requesting any chunk. It continues untouched
jobs and assembles only a complete acquisition. An existing destination is
reused only when this session has its original assembly receipt. A destination
that appears during acquisition is never overwritten; the completed chunks
remain available for a different path.

Each returned `ObjectDelivery` verifies its current file against the receipt and
extends the existing `VerifiedFile`: `bytes({limit})`, `json()`, `csvRows()`,
`chunks()`, `verify()` and create-only `saveAs()` work as for ordinary responses.
Buffered reads default to 8 MiB. Streaming uses fixed-size buffers and checks the
full digest while reading. Exhaust it before committing external effects: a
concurrent edit can be detected at the final check. `saveAs` publishes only the
complete verified copy.

`download.report.native` retains original progress; `download.report.process`
independently retains subprocess exit/error. `assembly` remains the original
receipt: `SAVED` at creation or `RECORDED` after reopen. The reader checks current
bytes even when the receipt records an earlier assembly. If the native engine
saved the file but could not record the receipt, `receiptRecorded` is false and
`assembly.receiptError` identifies the failure. Preserve that delivery and inspect
the same session; its chunks remain available without a new paid acquisition.

## Restart, cancellation and recovery

```js
const reopened = buyer.object('archive-october');
const progress = await reopened.inspect({chunkOffset: 0, chunkLimit: 50});
console.log(progress.native, progress.process);
await reopened.recover(); // Original saved-result recovery; no chunk request.
const file = await reopened.delivery('/private/customer/files/archive.zip');
await file.verify();

const imported = await buyer.attachObject({
  id: 'existing-archive', directory: '/private/original-object-session',
});
```

Only `run()` and `download()` can acquire new whole-file or chunk requests. `run()` returns progress
without assembly. `assemble(newPath)` assembles retained complete whole-file or
chunk responses offline.
`delivery(path?)` reopens the selected assembly or the latest recorded receipt.
These methods preserve the same original native intents and attempts.

`AbortSignal`, runtime timeout and CLI SIGINT/SIGTERM reach the original process.
`run()` preserves a valid interrupted report when produced. `download()` throws
`ObjectDownloadError` if it has progress without complete delivery:
`error.progress` contains that report and `error.acquisition` is the same handle.
Unavailable subprocess output raises `BuyerError` with its private
`commandDirectory` and acquisition. After the process exits, inspect/recover the
same session. `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` exposes the actual stopped chunk and
intent; use the original [queue recovery/finalization](../QUEUE.md) for that
intent. Do not resubmit it through a separate single-response `Operation`.

Named metadata and inputs are published together. After a lost response from
completed native preparation, `buyer.object(id).initialize()` binds and reopens
that same session. Interruption inside the native initializer before its
`session.json` exists retains an incomplete original directory; the API reports
`OBJECT_NATIVE_PREPARATION_INCOMPLETE` with its path. The native initializer owns
that recovery; the application neither deletes that state nor silently creates
another session. Keep absolute session, workspace, evidence and ledger paths in
place. Moving a session does not rebase its original bindings.

## Inspect and export

```js
for await (const acquisition of buyer.listObjects()) console.log(acquisition.id);
const page = await reopened.inspect({chunkOffset: 0, chunkLimit: 100});
console.log(page.chunks, page.chunkPage.nextOffset);
await reopened.exportReport('/private/customer/archive-review.html');
await reopened.exportReport('/private/customer/archive-report.json', {format: 'json'});
```

Results carry original scalar progress, one chunk page (default 50, maximum 250)
and the latest 25 assembly receipts. `chunkPage.nextOffset` pages a report;
`native.nextChunk` identifies the engine's next request. The full HTML or JSON
export includes every chunk and receipt through the original renderer, in a
private create-only file.

Native inspection reads completed object bytes even for a paged report. Reuse a
returned delivery for file consumption; export one full report to review many
chunks. Existing runtime `outputLimit` caps stdout/stderr at 1 MiB by default.
Use a smaller chunk page or a larger explicit runtime limit for unusually large
per-chunk metadata. Native byte, spending and terminal rules remain authoritative.

## Finish the original chunk accounting

File completion and financial state remain separate. The same application can
read or explicitly finish the original chunk reservations through the released
SF36/SF86 continuation:

```js
const accounting = await reopened.accounting({offset: 0, limit: 100});
console.log(accounting.native.entries, accounting.native.range.nextOffset);
const finalized = await reopened.finalize({
  workspaceDirectory: '/private/operator/archive', offset: 0, limit: 100,
});
console.log(finalized.native, finalized.process);
```

`accounting()` reads original retained views without re-reading product bytes.
`finalize()` invokes the original financial worker for these same native intents;
it can query configured providers and update the existing ledger. It never
requests another chunk. The original workspace, independently bound payer,
proof rules and ledger remain authoritative. Use the session's saved workspace,
or supply the matching original workspace when it was created from an explicit
configuration. Optional `outboxDirectory` and `merchantRoute` pass the existing
merchant evidence source to that original worker.

The returned `native` is the unchanged `session-accounting.v1` report, including
exact per-intent outcomes, prior finalization, source paths and native authority.
`range.nextOffset` continues the next explicit page (default 100, maximum 250).
Finalization is explicit and does not run on download. The command retains
process status independently; unresolved native outcomes remain visible for
the same original continuation.

Use `accountingPages()` or `finalizeAll()` to consume each native range through
one async iterator. `recoverAccounting()` reopens a retained command without a
provider request, and `exportAccounting()` writes all original accounting ranges
as a complete private JSONL export. The [shared customer accounting guide](ACCOUNTING.md)
documents cancellation, interrupted-command recovery and the installed commands.

## Installed command

The existing `starforge buyer-node` and `node forge.mjs run buyer-node -- ...`
entry points expose the same workflow. `buyer-node --help` lists required common
paths and exact options. `--object` is the customer name; `--object-id` selects
the merchant's descriptor alias.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `object-init` | Prepare from descriptor or explicit byte plan. |
| `object-attach` | Register `--session` under the customer's name. |
| `object-reopen` | Complete the name/session binding after a lost response. |
| `object-status` / `object-list` | Read native progress / list retained names. |
| `object-run` | Acquire untouched chunks without assembly. |
| `object-download --output FILE` | Preflight, continue and assemble/reopen this destination. |
| `object-recover` | Recover saved outcomes without new requests. |
| `object-assemble --output NEW_FILE` | Assemble complete chunks offline. |
| `object-verify [--output RECORDED_FILE]` | Reopen and verify a saved delivery. |
| `object-copy --output RECORDED_FILE --copy NEW_FILE` | Make a verified create-only copy. |
| `object-report --output NEW_FILE [--format html\|json]` | Export the complete original handoff. |
| `object-accounting [--offset N --limit N]` | Read original chunk financial views. |
| `object-finalize [--workspace BUYER_DIR]` | Explicitly finish the same original reservations. |

The command prints original progress/process status or the actual file/receipt.
An unresolved acquisition or process failure returns nonzero status and retains
the same session for continuation.

# Recover a buyer interrupted before approval

The Node buyer can continue the same prepared workspace-backed purchase after its native process ended before any original payment reservation. The recovery keeps the original intent, configuration, operator workspace and failed attempt, then starts one explicitly selected continuation through the original approval, reservation and signing path.

This is useful when a process or terminal disappears while the native buyer is waiting for the operator. First call the ordinary `recover()` method: a complete result may already be saved. When there is no native result, the recovery inspector checks the original process and the authenticated operator ledger before offering a continuation.

## Open the original operation

Use the same state directory, runtime directory and operator environment that prepared the purchase. Keep the complete published SDK and its original Python/native modules together.

```js
import { Buyer } from './node/index.mjs';

const buyer = await new Buyer({
  stateDirectory: '/private/customer-state',
  runtimeDirectory: '/installed/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  environment: process.env,
}).ready();

const operation = buyer.operation('original-request-id');
const saved = await operation.recover();
if (saved) {
  await saved.verify();
  // Read the already delivered result through saved.bytes(), json() or csvRows().
}
```

The operation's original `config.json`, request body and any operation ticket must still match their prepared hashes. A workspace-backed operation opens and audits its original workspace, keys, policy and ledger. It does not initialize another operator.

## Inspect the interrupted attempt

For attempts created by this release, the native runtime records the child PID, procfs PID, process birth ticks, PID namespace, host boot ID and procfs mount device. The inspector compares that exact identity with current process observations. A still-running process keeps ownership of its attempt.

```js
const available = await operation.inspectPreapprovalRecovery();
console.log(available.status, available.attemptSha256);
```

Earlier attempts may contain only a PID. A PID can be reused or refer to a different namespace, so those attempts need their **original native worker record**. Select the retained record and its exact request, process, output and driver hashes:

```js
const nativeRecord = {
  directory: '/private/original-native-record',
  hostRoot: '/installed/original-native-host',
  operationId: 'original-native-operation',
  requestSha256: '...64 lowercase hex characters...',
  processSha256: '...64 lowercase hex characters...',
  outputSha256: '...64 lowercase hex characters...',
  command: ['/installed/node', '/private/original-driver.mjs', '--original-option'],
  driverPath: '/private/original-driver.mjs',
  driverSha256: '...64 lowercase hex characters...',
};
const available = await operation.inspectPreapprovalRecovery({ nativeRecord });
```

The legacy adapter binds the actual original worker request, source driver, prepared review, workspace and final preapproval checkpoint. It invokes that installed worker's read-only inspector and verifies the original process namespace; caller-supplied hashes alone do not establish that the process ended. Preserve the native record and use its supported inspector instead of editing its state.

The returned `AVAILABLE` observation includes the original attempt/configuration hashes, private source pins, process proof and original ledger check. The ledger check is the existing SF36 authenticated audit under the original SF81 writer lock. It must find **zero reservations for this exact intent**, including terminal reservations. A reserved or paid intent follows its existing result/finality recovery path.

## Prepare one selected continuation

Choose the inspected attempt hash and record the reason. Preparation saves a fresh original offline review and a linked plan; it does not ask the signer to pay.

```js
const prepared = await operation.preparePreapprovalRecovery({
  expectedAttemptSha256: available.attemptSha256,
  nativeRecord, // Omit when the attempt's recorded process identity is sufficient.
  reason: 'Original terminal ended while waiting for approval.',
});
console.log(prepared.planSha256, prepared.review);
```

A changed attempt fails the expected-hash comparison. When a prior preparation completed but its return was lost, call the same preparation again or `readPreapprovalRecovery()`; the retained plan and review are returned. Review the saved plan before executing.

The original attempt remains at its original path. The new directory is:

```text
original-operation/
  operation.json
  config.json
  attempt.json
  review.json
  preapproval-continuation.json
  preapproval-history/
    <original-attempt-sha256>/
      original/
      process-request.json
      review.json
      plan.json
```

The archive preserves the exact original attempt, review, configuration, output descriptors and any empty response reservation. The plan pins those bytes and their original file identities. A completed process's old response lock is moved into that history only after fresh process and ledger checks, immediately before the new native output reservation. The original partial response must be empty.

## Execute through fresh approval

Pass the exact saved review and plan hash:

```js
const result = await operation.executePreapprovalRecovery({
  expectedPlanSha256: prepared.planSha256,
  review: prepared.review,
});
await result.verify();
```

Execution repeats the source, process and original ledger checks, exclusively records one linked child attempt, and launches the original SF88 native command. SF81 presents the actual current request for approval through the configured original broker or terminal. The operator's fresh request-specific approval still precedes the original durable reservation, signing and payment.

The SDK records the new native PID identity, private stdout/stderr and result in the child directory. It retains the same intent ID, response destination and original operator ledger. Ordinary `execute()` continues to reject an existing attempt, and calling `executePreapprovalRecovery()` twice cannot launch a second child.

The caller's abort signal and native runtime timeout apply to the new native process. Cancellation preserves the recorded attempt and output for inspection; it does not automatically launch again.

### Retain a failure before child creation

Metadata checks and the closed response-lock move complete before the exclusive child attempt. If this preparation is interrupted, executing the same selected plan recognizes the exact moved reservation inode and resumes the preparation. A new response writer at the original path causes a conflict.

After the child attempt is claimed, the runtime finishes descriptor and entry preparation before spawning. If it definitively fails before creating a child, the attempt becomes `NOT_DISPATCHED` with an embedded `stellar-forge.node-native-start-receipt.v1` receipt. That single saved record includes the original start time, observation time, phase, safe error code, exact native argv and its canonical SHA-256. An aborted call before spawn has the same explicit outcome when the receipt can be saved.

Inspect and prepare a new linked recovery for that selected failed attempt. The original ledger audit and fresh approval still apply. A missing or unwritable receipt leaves the existing claim intact; it never implies that no process ran.

Once a continuation is linked, ordinary `review()` returns that selected saved review and its original review time. It preserves the source review pinned by the recovery history.

## Reopen the same history and result

```js
const history = await operation.readPreapprovalRecovery();
const status = await operation.inspect();
const result = await operation.recover();
```

`inspect()` includes the original attempt state and selected preapproval history. `recover()` reads the selected child's saved result or complete native stdout using the original response verifier. It never launches a buyer. If the return was lost after payment, recover that original result and ledger outcome before considering any further action.

If a later child also ends before any reservation, its recorded process identity and the same authenticated zero-reservation audit can establish a new explicit recovery plan. Each child links to the exact hash of its parent attempt. Existing plan, archive and review bytes are checked on reopen.

## Useful diagnostics

| Code or outcome | Operator action |
| --- | --- |
| `PREAPPROVAL_RESULT_ALREADY_RECORDED` or `PREAPPROVAL_ORIGINAL_OUTPUT_EXISTS` | Reopen the original result/output. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_PROCESS_NOT_PROVEN_ABSENT` | Inspect the recorded process through its original runtime; preserve any active process. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` | Reopen the original workspace-backed operation. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_ORIGINAL_LEDGER_INSPECTOR_REQUIRED` | Install the complete matching SDK closure, including the original ledger module. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_ATTEMPT_CHANGED` | Inspect the selected attempt again before preparing. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_SOURCE_CHANGED` or `PREAPPROVAL_ARCHIVE_CHANGED` | Reconcile the original retained source/operation bytes. |
| `MATCHING_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | Use the exact review returned with the selected plan. |
| `ATTEMPT_ALREADY_RECORDED_USE_RECOVER` | Read the already recorded child instead of executing again. |

The helper's structured process diagnostics distinguish an active identity, different procfs scope, unavailable native authority and changed source. These checks use local process and retained native records; they do not contact a payment provider or alter the original worker.

## Retain metadata when storage is contended

A runtime configured with `nativeFileReservation` reserves backing on the actual metadata and output descriptors before starting the native child. The selected preapproval attempt uses four 65,536-byte metadata slots for its initial state, actual command, child identity and terminal state, plus the same saved-result bound used by ordinary execution and recovery. Closing an interrupted run can therefore publish its terminal checkpoint using already-held space. The configured provider and complete selected runtime source are described in [PROTECTED_STORAGE.md](PROTECTED_STORAGE.md).

The retained native command records the actual child invocation. When the protected bootstrap is selected, its private request binds the original entry file, original arguments, allocator descriptor and selected runtime source. The direct entry path keeps its original command shape.

## Retained wire history for the same intent

An interrupted native process can leave an unsigned request journal before the approval callback has returned. The normal preapproval workflow now carries that journal with the selected plan:

1. Inspection reads the complete private journal under its original writer lock. It accepts absent, pre-source and unsigned-only histories. A live writer or any signing/signed phase makes this preapproval path ineligible.
2. Preparation binds its complete file inventory and source digest into the immutable plan alongside the original attempt, review, configuration and native workspace.
3. Execution acquires the selected plan's own flock and repeats the original absent-process and authenticated zero-reservation ledger checks. It records that audit before changing the journal location.
4. The original journal directory moves intact to the plan's `original-wire/` directory. The actual source/phase bytes, temporary publication inodes and original writer lock are retained. `wire-selection.json` binds the plan, source attempt, exact inventory and audit; `wire-retirement.json` records the completed move. Both publication files use the existing held-file allocation provider when configured.
5. The caller reserves its four attempt-record replacements and result record, then enters the original runtime and its normal approval flow. The new journal occupies the original evidence pathname.


The same original journal lock protects cleanup of unused backing on its inventoried `.write-*` files. After the fresh process and original zero-reservation ledger audit, execution truncates each of those held descriptors to its existing logical length, syncs it, and rechecks its exact bytes, digest and inode. This releases abandoned `KEEP_SIZE` extents left by a killed writer while preserving the complete recorded inventory. It happens before transition metadata allocation; ordinary history reads remain read-only.

`readPreapprovalRecovery()` exposes the safe `wireHistory` projection for each retained plan. The original journal remains readable through its selected history even after a newer journal exists. Private request and authorization bytes remain in the original private evidence/history files.

An interruption before the directory move reopens the same selection and verifies the original journal. An interruption after the move verifies the exact archive and completes its existing retirement record. A competing or repeated execution cannot move the replacement journal: the per-plan lock, original attempt gate and immutable archive selection identify the old attempt independently of the canonical evidence pathname.

Preparation and execution continue to use the existing public methods and exact reviewed hashes. Existing plans without the additive wire inventory acquire their one immutable selection only after the same original process and ledger audit. The source configuration, operation ticket, original ledger and intent identifier retain their normal meanings.


| Wire outcome | Original operation action |
| --- | --- |
| `PREAPPROVAL_WIRE_WRITER_ACTIVE` | Read the original runtime and its active attempt before selecting another execution. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_RECOVERY_ACTIVE` | Reopen the same selected plan after its current caller finishes. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_NEW_WIRE_EXISTS` | Inspect the newer canonical attempt. The selected plan’s earlier journal remains in `original-wire/`. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_WIRE_SIGNING_OR_DISPATCH_RECORDED` | Use the existing authorization or lost-output recovery path appropriate to the recorded phase. |
| `PREAPPROVAL_WIRE_SOURCE_CHANGED` | Reopen the original plan and compare its retained inventory with the current source before selecting a continuation. |

# Native buyer for Node applications

Go applications can use the complete [native Go buyer](../go/README.md) and
`starforge-buyer` executable against this same selected runtime and original
application state. Its customer workflow covers operations, Inbox commerce,
whole and chunked objects, typed datasets, and retained SSE/NDJSON responses.

The complete [acquisition workflow](ACQUISITIONS.md) joins private merchant
requests, explicit receiver review, original operator preparation, immutable
runbooks, native execution/accounting, verified downloads and recovery of every
original operator journal. Use `AcquisitionWorkspace` directly or
`buyer.acquisitions(...)`; Node and Python share the same original bridge.

This package connects an application to the **existing SF88 operator buyer**. It
also fits the original SF30 generated client's `createSellerClient({ buyer })`
interface. It does not implement a signer, approve payments, decide settlement,
replace the SF36 ledger, or automatically retry a purchase.

The complete path is: saved catalog or generated API request -> private immutable
operation -> original offline review -> one original native attempt -> durable
output -> verified application data. Cancellation and restart recovery retain the
original intent. A process crash does not authorize another attempt.

The same Buyer also handles persistent dataset acquisition and verified SF100
rows, described below, and the complete [large-file object workflow](OBJECTS.md).
`createObject`/`attachObject` retain a native chunk acquisition; `download`,
`recover`, `assemble` and `delivery` return the original progress and verified
file to the customer application. The existing `buyer-node` command includes
the matching `object-*` lifecycle, without a new package or payment engine.
`accounting` and explicit `finalize` invoke the original chunk reservation
continuation and return its native report separately from file completion.

The complete [dataset and object accounting workflow](ACCOUNTING.md) reads or
finalizes every original page/chunk range, reports progress to an async consumer,
stops on cancellation, reopens saved native command output after a process loss,
and streams the complete financial view to a new private JSONL file. These methods
use the same native sessions and are usable independently of delivered data files.

Finite SSE and NDJSON responses use the same native operation and retained file.
Select `responseFile.stream` before review, then consume verified records with
`result.events()` or `result.ndjson()`. Reopen them after a restart with
`operation.recover()`. The [streaming application guide](STREAMS.md) covers both
completed responses and retained complete records from an interrupted transfer.

The complete [customer inbox workflow](INBOX.md) joins merchant packet or
generated-client intake to the original private SF88 queue. Review several
saved requests, execute one selected intent through native terminal approval,
cancel an unattempted job, recover after interruption, consume its verified
file or stream, and finalize/export the original history. A transferred Node
operation stays bound to that one inbox. The same `buyer-node` command exposes
the entire `inbox-*` workflow, with complete private handover and reopening.

## Install and runtime

Node 22 or later is required. There are no npm dependencies or install scripts.
Use the package directly from this checkout, or install it into an application:

```sh
npm install --ignore-scripts /absolute/checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/node
```

This is a source/local package; this change does not claim an npm registry release.
The **original complete Stellar Forge runtime** must remain installed separately.
`runtimeDirectory` is the absolute path to `sf88-operator-buyer-cli`, not the
repository root. Original native dependencies, Python policy/ledger, operator
configuration and signing setup remain as documented in the parent README and
NATIVE_SIGNER.md. No credentials are downloaded or embedded by this package.

Use a private caller-owned state directory (0700 on POSIX). Do not share it between
untrusted OS users. Windows requires an appropriately restricted directory ACL;
the package does not configure Windows ACLs. Linux is the exercised platform.

## Existing private SF88 config

```js
import { Buyer } from '@stellar-forge/native-buyer';

const buyer = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory: '/srv/forge/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  stateDirectory: '/srv/private/customer-purchases',
});
const operation = await buyer.fromConfig('/srv/private/operator.json');
const review = await operation.review();
console.log(review.native); // Offline terms and request/body fingerprint only.
const result = await operation.execute({ review });
result.raiseForStatus();
const data = await result.json();
```

`fromConfig` copies request bytes and records their hash. The native evidence and
saved response paths are relocated into the new operation's private directory;
response limits, content pins and selected stream format are retained. Original operator/policy/ledger/signer
paths are not copied or reimplemented. To export a completed download use
`result.saveAs('/absolute/new-file')`, which never overwrites an existing file.
Merchant `ticketFile` bytes are validated by original SF88, copied privately and

```js
console.log(acquisition.native.status, acquisition.process);
if (acquisition.native.status !== 'COMPLETE') {
  // Display the original limits, stoppedPage and next guidance to the operator.

const rows = await delivery.readRows(); // fully verified before returning
```

accepted terms. An optional original operator profile is applied only to this
configuration source. A workspace always supplies its own original configuration
and keys; application profiles do not override it.

The `expectedSnapshot` option binds an explicitly selected native snapshot. When
it is omitted, an existing `snapshot` URL parameter is preserved. New acquisitions
use the original shared SF88/SF100 limits: 1–4,096 pages, 1–1,000,000 rows,
1,024–2,097,152 bytes per page, and a positive decimal atomic-unit allocation
ceiling. The original runtime validates these values before creating a native
session; this SDK does not maintain a separate policy. Existing native sessions
retain their original read/recovery compatibility. Total allocations and actual
charges are separate values; the original ledger and evidence retain financial

```js

const state = await existing.recover();
console.log(state.native); // original recovery: no HTTP, signing or purchase
if (state.native.status === 'READY') {
  // Explicit continuation: acquire only pages the original engine has not tried.
  await existing.run();
}
const delivery = await existing.deliver(); // same default destination resumes
console.log(delivery.report.resumed, delivery.report.appendedPages);
```

session must finish before attachment because the original status contract then
returns only `RUNNING`, without its immutable identity. Recovery uses the original

new page controller. Do not move a native session after creation.

`initialize()` is an offline continuation after a lost creation/attachment
response. It checks the original source binding and reuses a complete original
session. The application entry is staged with complete private metadata before
its stable name is published; leftover `.dataset-stage-*` directories are private
preparation remnants and are ignored by the acquisition list. If the original
creation itself was interrupted before publishing a
valid `session.json`, the native error and private files remain available; no
purchase could have started through this initialization command. Run and recover
never silently change the saved configuration, expected snapshot or limits.

Pass `{signal}` to `run`, `inspect`, `recover`, `initialize`, `exportManifest`, or
as the second argument of `deliver`. Dataset commands use the original Node
SDK's native child, environment, timeout, output limit and cleanup grace.
The original `emitPageSummaries:false` option suppresses repeated page stdout;
the default 1 MiB stdout/stderr budget is separate from `datasetReportLimit`,
which defaults to 32 MiB and accepts 1–256 MiB. A report exceeding that limit
returns `DATASET_REPORT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` after retaining the original session;
reopen with a larger report limit to inspect the saved outcome. The native page
and total acquisition limits still apply. A stop
reaches the original acquisition's AbortSignal. Its current native page may need
original reconciliation after interruption; a new `run()` never repeats a marked
page. An application crash does not destroy the separate original session.

Each completed command returns `{native, process}`. `native` is the original
report; `process` contains `exitCode`, `exitSignal` and `errorCode`. A clean stop
can return a useful partial original report alongside an abort error. If no
complete result was published, the error identifies `commandDirectory`; its
private native logs are retained. Successful commands retain the latest complete

per-page summaries, so it is not parsed as one artificial acquisition object.
The separate atomic report contains the original API return value.

## Recovery, concurrency and cancellation

```js
const existing = buyer.operation('report-001');
const saved = await existing.recover(); // No spawn, signer or HTTP call.
if (saved) await saved.saveAs('/srv/private/recovered-report.json');
console.log(await existing.inspect());
```

Every intent has a SHA-256-named directory. Creation is exclusive. Immediately
before launch, an fsynced atomic exclusive `attempt.json` records that the attempt
has started. Concurrent processes cannot both publish this marker. It does not
expire, and failed/timed-out/interrupted attempts are never automatically rerun.
Repeated `call()` with the same intent returns an explicit error pointing to
recovery; it does not silently issue a second request or assume an equivalent
request. Recovery also refuses changed configuration and body bytes.

Native stdout/stderr go directly to private files so a still-running native child
can finish recording its summary after an application-parent crash. If a complete
summary exists without a durably recorded process exit, recovery preserves
`PROCESS_EXIT_NOT_RECORDED` and `exitCode: null`. A valid saved file may still be
consumed. This is not a claim that settlement or process success was proven.
Partial/missing output remains recoverable only when the original native process
actually finishes; `recover()` does not fabricate a result.

Use one `AbortController` for the whole application task:

```js
const controller = new AbortController();
const { signal } = controller;
const operation = await buyer.fromRequest(request, { signal });
const review = await operation.review({ signal });
const result = await operation.execute({ review, signal });
// A Stop action calls controller.abort(); await the task before closing its workspace.
```

Preparation accepts `{signal}` in `fromConfig`, `fromWorkspace`,
`fromOperationHandoff`, and `prepare`. A generated `fromRequest` or `call`
accepts either `request.signal` or `options.signal`; when both are supplied,
aborting either stops the task. `call` carries the same combined signal through
preparation, offline review, and its original execution. A signal that is already
aborted is rejected before creating an operation or launching a review child.
The signal is an in-memory task control and is never written into the operation.

When preparation is cancelled, the creating call drains its native review and
removes its own unpublished operation. The same intent can then be prepared
again. Cancelling `operation.review({signal})` retains the already prepared
operation, so the application can review it again using a fresh signal.
Cancelling execution retains its original attempt and uses the recovery workflow
above. A workspace Stop/close handler should abort and await the active task
before releasing its lease.

On abort/timeout the SDK sends SIGTERM to its own tracked native child, waits for
`close`, and allows the
configured cleanup grace (default 15 seconds). If the native child does not exit,
it sends SIGKILL and records `NATIVE_CLEANUP_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. It does not promise
that forced termination reconciles payment or kills arbitrary grandchildren.
Original durable ledger/evidence remains authoritative. No stale PID is killed
by a later recovery call. On Windows process signals are forceful, so graceful
POSIX cleanup guarantees do not apply.

Default native timeout is 360 seconds and per-stream retained output budget is 1 MiB (100 ms sampling during execution).
Oversized logs are truncated after child exit and invalidate the result.
Private native logs are never embedded in application error messages. Configure
`environment` explicitly when the application should pass a reduced environment.
The default preserves the caller's original signer/operator environment.

`BuyerError` and its subclasses format as an error code, stack, and the public
`exitCode` and `destinationPublished` fields when available. `JSON.stringify`
uses the same public fields through `error.toJSON()`. Recovery objects, saved
results, paths and other private details remain directly accessible through
`error.operation`, `error.dataset`, `error.acquisition` and their existing
properties, but are non-enumerable and excluded from default diagnostic output.
Use those handles to reopen the existing operation after handling the error.

## Data consumption and integrity

A `BuyerResult` preserves the native summary, exit status, recovery marker and
response-file metadata separately. `ok` is native process/HTTP success, **not an
independent on-chain finality certificate**. `raiseForStatus()` is optional when
recovering useful saved data after an evidence/cleanup failure. Inspect the
original outcome report for its authoritative classification.

`bytes()` and `json()` verify size/SHA-256 completely before returning data; the
default memory limit is 8 MiB. `verify()` hashes without buffering. `chunks()` and
`csvRows()` first verify the saved file and verify again while streaming, using
no-follow file opens and size/time checks. Exhaust the iterator before committing
external side effects; concurrent same-user mutation can still cause a final
integrity error after earlier chunks/rows were consumed. Early iterator return
closes its descriptor but is not a full-stream verification.

`csvRows({ headers: true })` handles UTF-8/BOM, quoted commas/newlines, escaped
quotes, CRLF and chunk boundaries. Duplicate/empty headers, differing column
counts, invalid UTF-8 and malformed quoted fields are rejected. It yields string
records without numeric coercion; plain `csvRows()` yields arrays. Field length
is limited to 1 MiB of characters by default. `saveAs` streams to a private
partial file and publishes the destination only after complete digest validation.

The state format is `stellar-forge.node-buyer.v1`; it is intentionally separate
from the Python package's format. Both use the same original native financial
ledger when configured to do so, but their application state directories and
attempt markers must not be interchanged. Filesystem durability assumes a local
filesystem supporting atomic hard links and fsync; network/distributed filesystems
require their own validation.

## Explicit continuation after an unpaid transport failure

When the original native buyer records `INITIAL_TRANSPORT_FAILED` before any
signature, the application can preserve that result and prepare one explicit
successor after correcting the connection. For example, a merchant's existing
CA bundle may need to be included in the native child environment. Continue to
verify the merchant hostname and certificate chain, and retain the original
operator, ledger, signer, URL, request bytes and accepted terms.

`operation.recover()` always returns the original operation's saved outcome.
Use the following separate preparation call when the application operator has
selected a continuation:

```js
const original = buyer.operation('customer-report-2026-10-11');
const status = await original.inspectUnpaidContinuation();
if (!status.eligible) throw new Error(status.reason);

const successor = await original.prepareUnpaidContinuation({
  intentId: 'customer-report-2026-10-11-transport-repaired',
  expectedResultSha256: status.resultSha256,
  reason: 'Included the existing merchant CA and verified the unchanged HTTPS endpoint.',
  signal,
});

// Existing terminal approval, original policy and native attempt gate all apply.
const result = await successor.execute({
  review: await successor.review({ signal }),
  signal,
});
const data = await result.json();
```

Preparation requires the exact final result digest, the chosen successor ID and
a recorded remediation reason. It checks the original recorded process exit,
native stdout, original checkout evidence and outcome report together. Eligibility
requires the native initial-transport failure, explicit `paymentSent: false`,
zero signature/transfer/uncertain outcomes and no operator reservation or response
file. The request, body, operation ticket, operator configuration and native
workspace remain bound to their original bytes and settings.

One immutable `unpaid-continuation.json` chooses the successor under the original
private descriptor/flock serialization pattern. Its ready record binds the
successor's prepared configuration and metadata before that successor can execute.
Repeating preparation with the same ID, result digest and reason returns that
same operation. Selecting a different successor for that parent fails with
`UNPAID_CONTINUATION_ALREADY_SELECTED`. A process interruption during preparation
retains the partial private files and resumes the same chosen ID; a completed
preparation or native attempt is reopened. Linux util-linux `flock` is required
for this explicit feature.

To resume an application, follow an already prepared lineage and recover its
actual selected operation:

```js
const active = await buyer.operation('customer-report-2026-10-11')
  .followUnpaidContinuation();
let result = await active.recover();
if (result === null && (await active.inspect()).state === 'PREPARED') {
  result = await active.execute({ review: await active.review({ signal }), signal });
}
```

`followUnpaidContinuation()` is read-only. It validates each existing parent and
successor binding; it does not select a successor, prepare an operation, authorize
a payment or execute a buyer. The research page fetcher uses this same following
method before its normal recovery and execution path, so the saved logical page
request and edition cursor survive a corrected transport. Every successor still
has its own nonreplaceable native attempt marker. A further continuation requires
another explicit call against an eligible final outcome.

The original failed result, attempt, evidence and configuration remain available
under their original ID. Errors with a missing final process outcome, possible
signature, reservation, response or uncertain transfer must use their existing
native recovery/accounting path.

~~~js
  directory: '/private/customer/operator',
  stateRoot: '/private/customer',
  inboxes: ['/private/customer/inbox'],
  include: ['/private/customer/python-app'],
};
const inspected = await recovery.inspect(selection);
console.log(inspected.native.selected);
console.log(inspected.native.inboxes);
~~~

Inspection reads the existing original workspace and inbox. It reports selected
roots, missing optional outputs, runtime dependencies, original job identities
and states. It does not export wallet values or execute an operation. A standalone
new WorkspaceRecovery({ runtimeDirectory }) provides the same methods when
there is no live Buyer object; its constructor creates no state.

## Stop writers, capture, and independently verify

Stop the real inbox, CLI, browser, SDK and other writers before capture. The
quiesced flag records that operating action; it does not stop processes.
The native worker additionally holds its original reservation while taking a
consistent SQLite snapshot and rejects a source that changes during capture.

Set the passphrase in a selected environment variable through the host's private
secret mechanism before constructing the runtime. The API accepts only its
NAME: passphraseEnv defaults to SF88_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE. It never accepts the
passphrase as a method argument, command argument or result. The native engine
requires a separate 16–65536-byte passphrase and refuses the configured wallet
variable and the original three SF36 key variable names.

The output must be a new directory outside stateRoot; its existing parent must
be canonical. Node's temporary native logs are private directories beside
stateRoot for inspection/capture and under the existing OS temporary directory
for verification/restore. The bundle parent can remain read-only. Logs are removed
after the original process finishes. No SDK operation
log is written into the quiesced source.

~~~js
const saved = await recovery.snapshot({
  ...selection,
  output: '/private/backups/customer-2026-10-11',
  quiesced: true,
  passphraseEnv: 'SF88_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE',
});
const expectedRecordSha256 = saved.native.recordSha256;
// Retain this exact digest in the application's existing backup inventory.
const verified = await recovery.verify({
  bundle: saved.native.bundle,
  expectedRecordSha256,
  python: '/usr/bin/python3',
});
console.log(verified.native.checkpoint, verified.native.inboxes);
~~~

Verification independently authenticates and decrypts the archive, checks the
original file inventory and the original SF36 journal, and removes its temporary
plaintext. python selects the current trusted absolute verification interpreter,
not a program named by archive contents. It does not rewrite saved runtime paths.
Install the retained runtime dependencies at their original locations before
resuming normal operator work.

## Restore first, then reopen the original applications

Select the verified archive and its independently retained record digest. The
original canonical state root must be absent or an empty private directory.
The original engine refuses populated state; preserve and reconcile any newer
history through the existing operating process before choosing a backup.
There is no destination override or automatic deletion/merge.

Construct the standalone recovery handle before a Buyer or any other initializer
can recreate missing state. The example below belongs to that recovery process;
it does not move or remove a currently operating workspace.

~~~js
const recovery = new WorkspaceRecovery({ runtimeDirectory, environment: process.env });
const restored = await recovery.restore({
  bundle: '/private/backups/customer-2026-10-11',
  expectedRecordSha256, // Loaded from the existing trusted backup inventory.
  python: '/usr/bin/python3',
});
console.log(restored.native.stateRoot, restored.native.checkpoint);

const reopened = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory,
  stateDirectory: '/private/customer/node-app',
});
const operation = reopened.operation('the-original-saved-intent');
const status = await operation.inspect();
const response = await operation.recover(); // Saved local result; no new attempt.
~~~

The native restore publishes the complete original state and reopens its operator
and inbox. Pending jobs stay pending. Permanent attempts, request fingerprints,
keys, evidence, outputs and accounting history retain their original identity.
Restoring does not execute a queue, finalize an attempt or load a wallet secret.

The same restored Python application directory can be reopened with its existing
Python Buyer and saved intent IDs; do not point it at the Node application
directory. Native dataset/object/runbook directories reopen through their original
client APIs. The recovered directory names and source pointers are not rewritten.

## Process outcomes and interruption

Successful calls return WorkspaceRecoveryResult with native completion metadata
and a separate process receipt. An invalid result, native error, timeout or
cancellation throws WorkspaceRecoveryError. Its result retains recognized native
metadata, exitCode, exitSignal, errorCode, whether a process started, and any
temporary-log cleanup error. No raw stdout, stderr or environment values are
included in the error message.

~~~js
const controller = new AbortController();
try {
  await recovery.verify({
    bundle: '/private/backups/customer-2026-10-11',
    expectedRecordSha256,
    signal: controller.signal,
  });
} catch (error) {
  if (!(error instanceof WorkspaceRecoveryError)) throw error;
  console.log(error.code, error.result.process, error.result.completionReported);
  // Inspect the reported native completion and actual original state before
  // deciding how to continue. Never delete or repeat a restore automatically.
}
~~~

The existing NativeRuntime sends SIGTERM on AbortSignal or timeout, allows its
configured cleanupGraceMs, then uses SIGKILL if necessary. The original snapshot,
verification and restore engine honors its native cancellation signal. Inspection
is read-only and does not poll that signal internally; its process still remains
under the runtime's deadline and termination control.

A process can be interrupted after an atomic archive or state publication.
completionReported means the original completion was received; false means it
was not received, not that the filesystem is unchanged. If the original completed
result is present despite a process/cleanup error, it remains in error.result.native.
The SDK never rolls back, deletes, merges, re-executes or blindly retries that
state. Use the original inspection/reopen path and the selected archive to resolve
the actual outcome.

# Consume an original paid SSE or NDJSON response in Node

The existing `Buyer` prepares one original SF88 operation, retains its complete
configuration and executes the native approval/signing/accounting path. Add
`responseFile.stream` to capture a finite event response. The same operation's
`BuyerResult` reads its saved records and reopens after a process restart.

The package uses the shared parser from the selected original runtime. Install
the package with its matching SCF runtime source, as described in [README](README.md).

## Prepare, execute and read

```js
import { Buyer } from '@stellar-forge/native-buyer';

const buyer = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory: '/absolute/installed/source/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  stateDirectory: '/absolute/private/customer',
  operatorProfile: '/absolute/private/operator-profile.json',
});

const operation = await buyer.fromRequest({
  intentId: 'forecast-events-2026-10-11',
  url: 'https://seller.example/forecast-events',
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ region: 'northeast' }),
  expect: {
    scheme: 'exact', network: 'stellar:testnet',
    asset: 'THE_SELECTED_TOKEN_CONTRACT', payTo: 'THE_SELECTED_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT',
    maxAtomic: '50000', paymentFlow: 'upfront',
  },
}, {
  requestTimeoutMs: 180000,
  responseFile: {
    maxBytes: 67108864, timeoutMs: 120000,
    stream: { format: 'sse', maxRecordBytes: 1048576, maxRecords: 100000 },
  },
});

const result = await operation.execute({ review: await operation.review(), signal });
result.raiseForStatus();
for await (const event of result.events()) {
  console.log(event.index, event.event, event.data, event.id);
}
```

Use the actual observed merchant URL, asset, recipient, amount and intended flow.
An absent payment flow still means `authorization`. The selected `upfront` flow
must also be configured in the original operator workspace signer; initialize the
workspace from the reviewed operation using the maintained workspace command.
The native terminal and existing budget policy handle its approval.

The reviewed `requestTimeoutMs` bounds each complete merchant HTTP exchange,
including DNS, TLS, provider generation, response headers and body consumption.
Its range is 1–300000 milliseconds. `responseFile.timeoutMs` separately bounds
capture after the response returns. An omitted request deadline defaults to the
selected stream timeout; ordinary requests default to 30000 milliseconds. The
`Buyer` constructor's existing `timeoutMs` bounds the whole native subprocess,
including operator interaction and accounting.

`responseFile` options also work with `fromConfig`, `fromOperationHandoff`,
`prepare`, and `call(request, options)`. The Node application chooses the fixed
`response.bin` inside its private operation directory. Local expected byte count,
content type and SHA-256 survive into the original native writer. Callers cannot
replace the application's destination through these options.

For generated seller clients, compose the same `call` interface:

```js
const applicationBuyer = {
  call: request => buyer.call(request, {
    responseFile: {
      timeoutMs: 120000,
      stream: { format: 'ndjson', maxRecords: 50000 },
    },
  }),
};
// Pass applicationBuyer as the existing generated client's buyer option.
```

The original response is captured as it arrives. `execute()` resolves after the
native operation and capture complete. For live record callbacks during a trusted
embedded SF31 request, use the original
[`prepareBuyerResponseFile().save(..., { onRecord })` API](../../sf31-buyer-client/STREAMING.md).
The Node process API exposes the retained result after its original subprocess
has completed.

## Read NDJSON and reopen the same operation

Choose `stream: { format: 'ndjson' }` for an NDJSON response:

```js
const reopened = await buyer.operation('inventory-stream-2026-10-11').recover();
if (!reopened) throw new Error('The original operation has no retained result yet');
reopened.raiseForStatus();
for await (const row of reopened.ndjson()) {
  await consumeRow(row);
}
```

`events()` yields standard SSE records. `ndjson<T>()` yields each parsed JSON
value. JSON numbers use JavaScript's normal numeric semantics; a merchant should
encode identifiers and precision-sensitive amounts as strings. The raw original
bytes and digest remain available through inherited `chunks()`, `bytes()`,
`verify()` and `saveAs()`.

These readers verify the complete retained file before yielding any record, and
check the bytes again during consumption. Exhaust the iterator before committing
whole-response side effects. Changing the saved file, an invalid media type,
malformed framing or an unfinished final record returns a concrete reader error.
Reading a result never starts the native buyer.

## Inspect the completed prefix of a failed capture

Cancellation uses the same `AbortSignal` already accepted by `execute()`. The
native writer retains its private partial bytes, their SHA-256, record count and
last complete frame boundary in the original summary. Reopen the operation and
opt into partial inspection:

```js
const original = await buyer.operation('forecast-events-2026-10-11').recover();
if (original?.delivery.status === 'FAILED' && original.stream) {
  for await (const event of original.events({ allowPartial: true })) {
    await inspectRetainedEvent(event);
  }
}
```

The reader verifies the entire recorded partial-file digest, then exposes only
the original `lastCompleteByte` prefix. Incomplete UTF-8, half a JSON record and
an undispatched SSE event remain outside that prefix. The native result retains
its failure and accounting state. Reuse the same intent and original recovery
record when addressing the interruption.

From the Node package directory, prepare the immutable operation and review it:

The example cap is 10000 atomic units; choose the cap authorized for your actual

The payload mapping follows the [official Answer API](https://exa.ai/docs/reference/answer)
and [Exa's SDK at commit 443071918171](https://github.com/exa-labs/exa-js/blob/4430719181718117889247dc31bd5cd9e7ca459b/src/index.ts).
Only the original paid merchant operation acquires data; both recovery and the
application helper consume its retained response.

## Limits and record meaning

Defaults are 64 MiB for the whole capture, 1 MiB per record, 100000 records, and
30 seconds. Original native streaming transport accepts a selected total duration
up to five minutes. Use `maxRecordBytes` and `maxRecords` on the reader to choose
additional local consumption limits. None of these values changes the offered
price or the original spending reservation.

SSE preserves `event`, multiline `data`, persistent `id`, and numeric `retry`
metadata. It supports LF, CRLF and lone CR; comments and unknown fields are
ignored. NDJSON requires newline-terminated UTF-8 JSON values and ignores empty
lines. Both preserve the original raw file. IDs and retry metadata are exposed
for the application to inspect; these readers perform no automatic reconnect.

# Continue a reserved authorization that never reached dispatch

A native attempt can lose its filesystem after receiving the original payment-required response, or after creating an authorization in memory, before the signed request is sent. The original transport recorder distinguishes that state from a request whose delivery is uncertain. `Operation.prepareUndispatchedContinuation()` prepares one explicitly selected successor from the retained original request. The successor uses the original Node Buyer review, operator approval, reservation and execution path.

This continuation applies to an interrupted direct Node operation whose final native result or evidence was not fully recorded. The source reader must establish all of the following from the existing files:

- The original operation, configuration, request body, ticket and attempt still have their recorded identities.
- The full native wire reader acquires the original writer lock and validates every retained record. The writer is inactive and there is no signed-dispatch record.
- The actual generated workspace signer uses the reviewed original environment signer and authorization flow. Its complete source chain is recognized and hash-bound.
- The original approved request and accepted payment terms match the retained signing input. If the signer was never entered, the original SF31 client reconstructs that input from the retained unsigned 402 response using the same request and term-selection logic; the original SF54 mapper must produce the exact approved request.
- The original SF36 HMAC audit returns this same request in the `reserved` state, with actual amount zero and empty receipt and proof references.

When signing was entered, the signer may have created an authorization in memory. The source snapshot preserves that distinction from the earlier response-only boundary. The original authorization path builds, simulates and signs; the paid merchant request is performed by the later guarded transport. The durable dispatch marker precedes that transport. The validated absence of this marker supplies the relevant execution boundary.

## Two original transport boundaries

| Retained wire state | Original input used by the reader | Returned authorization scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SIGNING_STARTED_NOT_DISPATCHED`, or another validated state after signing began with no signed dispatch | The exact retained `signing-input` and the reviewed native authorization source | `signedAuthorizationMayExist: true` |
| `UNSIGNED_RESPONSE_HEADERS_RETAINED`, with no signing records | The original unsigned 402 response, request URL, method, headers and exact body, passed through the original SF31 client | `signedAuthorizationMayExist: false` |

The earlier 402 reader supplies a single retained response to the original SF31 transport and captures its immutable approval intent with a callback that always declines. It provides no real network transport and never invokes the signer. The original SF54/SF36 mapping then verifies the caller's supplied approved request and SHA256. Both paths re-read the complete inactive wire and original source identities before returning.

The returned `signerSources` is a map from each source role to its exact path, byte count and SHA256. Existing signing-input snapshots keep their original values and canonical digest when the earlier-gate support is installed.

## Select the existing operation

Open the same original runtime, state directory and private operator workspace. An existing mixed lineage can be followed without preparing anything:

```js
import {Buyer} from './node/client.mjs';

const buyer = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory: '/absolute/original/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  stateDirectory: '/absolute/customer/buyer-state',
});

const root = buyer.operation('original-intent');
const interrupted = await root.followContinuation();
const status = await interrupted.inspect();
console.log({
  intentId: interrupted.intentId,
  state: status.state,
  resultRecoverable: status.resultRecoverable,
  checkpoint: status.transportCheckpoint?.state,
});
```

The full inspection reopens the recorder on disk. A stdout summary alone is insufficient: an atomic write can publish its final filename before directory synchronization fails. Reading the actual record set handles that case.

## Prepare the chosen successor

Use the exact original approved request preimage, the original attempt-file SHA256 and its configuration SHA256. Select the successor ID once and reuse it if preparation is interrupted.

```js
const next = await interrupted.prepareUndispatchedContinuation({
  intentId: 'original-intent-undispatched-continuation-1',
  expectedRequestSha256: originalApprovedRequestSha256,
  expectedAttemptId: originalAttemptFileSha256,
  expectedConfigSha256: originalConfigurationSha256,
  approvedRequestFile: '/absolute/private/original-approved-request.json',
  workspace: '/absolute/original/operator-workspace',
  reason: 'The filesystem is writable again; the recorded authorization never reached dispatch.',
});

const review = await next.review();
const result = await next.execute({review});
```

The execution opens the original operator approval prompt. Its request, amount, payer, merchant, request body and timeout retain the original settings. Only the chosen intent ID and SDK-owned destination paths move. A configured buyer profile cannot silently replace the parent's policy, ledger, signer or transport during successor creation.

The method accepts either `approvedRequest` or `approvedRequestFile`. Object inputs are copied before asynchronous work. Optional `node`, `environment` and `signal` retain the same native worker and cancellation contracts used by the original expired continuation. An expiry artifact is not an input to this method.

## Reopen after interruption

The parent owns `undispatched-continuation.json`, its immutable source-bound choice, and `undispatched-continuation-ready.json`, the completed child binding. The same parent descriptor lock serializes unpaid, expired and undispatched choices.

Calling preparation again with the same selected ID, original source and reason reopens the same child. If the child was interrupted while being prepared, its unfinished files are preserved under an original state-directory preparation name and that same selected child is prepared again. A child with an attempt cannot be replaced through this path.

After a ready binding exists, `followContinuation()` follows it without preparing, approving or executing. The original research page adapter already uses this method, so resuming the same edition reaches the chosen operation and keeps the original cursor and provider request.

```js
const reopened = new Buyer({runtimeDirectory, stateDirectory});
const active = await reopened.operation(originalIntentId).followContinuation();
const retained = await active.recover();
const selection = await interrupted.inspectUndispatchedContinuation();
```

The existing unpaid and expiry source predicates remain separate. Old metadata and choices reopen with their original schemas.

## Accounting and retained files

The original SF36 reservation remains in the original ledger. Preparation performs a read-only HMAC-verified reservation lookup. It neither settles the original reservation at zero nor alters historical accounting. The successor must pass ordinary fresh approval and budget admission when executed.

The choice binds the original native source/output hashes, approved request, full recorder snapshot, reviewed signer source identities and audited reservation. Its ready file binds the child's operation, configuration, body and ticket. Every later original `_bound()` validates this lineage before review, recovery or execution.

The authorization source reader returns a safe metadata snapshot. Signed payloads, keys and private wire bodies stay in the original private operation directory. The ordinary inspector and continuation status expose source hashes and phase metadata.

## Actual receiving case

The first receiving case is a retained research page operation. Its previous expiry successor entered the original signer, then encountered `ENOSPC`. The native stdout survived while the final SDK result file did not. The full recorder read returned `SIGNING_STARTED_NOT_DISPATCHED`, an inactive writer, and four records ending at `signing-input`. This path turns those recorded facts into the next source-bound original operation while preserving the earlier reservations and accepted source pages.

A second actual receiving case retained the unsigned 402 headers and the original operator-approved request before `ENOSPC` prevented entry to the signer. The reader reconstructed the exact original request, returned `UNSIGNED_RESPONSE_HEADERS_RETAINED` with `signingEntered: false`, and retained the preceding case's snapshot byte-for-byte. Preparing another successor still requires the original reserved-row audit and usable destination storage.

## Explicit source adoption for a protected successor

When the original failure requires a reviewed source change, preserve the parent's canonical runtime and select a complete distinct runtime with `successorRuntime: {directory, sourceManifestFile, sourceManifestSha256}`. The immutable choice binds that full source manifest. The selected runtime supplies its own Buyer, Store and original native execution; all request, body, ticket and operator checks still apply. An existing native-workspace import retains its separate original command adoption contract.

`await buyer.openOperation(savedIntentId)` reopens one exact recorded child in that explicitly selected runtime. It neither prepares a successor nor follows later children. Existing `operation(id)` remains synchronous and `followContinuation()` retains its lineage behavior.

[Protected native storage and runtime adoption](./PROTECTED_STORAGE.md) documents the actual-FD provider, manifest, parent preservation, source checks and same-edition research receiving path.

# Native operator workspace customer

Use `Buyer.fromWorkspace` when the original SF88 operator has already been initialized.
The native workspace owns the signer, payer, policy, ledger, private evidence,
transport and approved payment limits. The Node application owns its prepared
request, response destination and single permanent attempt. Existing
`fromConfig` and `fromRequest` applications keep their original behavior.

The package calls the installed original application bridge. Its historical
`ORIGINAL_PYTHON_WORKSPACE` mode name is retained for compatibility; the same
bridge now serves both customer languages. No workspace keys are returned to the
application, copied into its metadata or passed through public command arguments.
The signer still uses the operator process's existing wallet environment.

## Prepare from the existing operator

Initialize an operator using the original `cli.mjs --init-workspace`
instructions and exact reviewed request. For a partially initialized
runbook-owned operator, use the original [runbook recovery workflow](../../buyer-runbook/WORKSPACE.md)
and its explicit resume action. `Buyer.fromWorkspace` requires an initialized
workspace and preserves its wallet, policy and ledger. The original
`--review-workspace` and `--diagnose-workspace` commands remain the setup view.

```js
import { Buyer } from '@stellar-forge/native-buyer';

const buyer = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory: '/srv/starforge/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  stateDirectory: '/srv/private/customer-app',
});
const operation = await buyer.fromWorkspace('/srv/private/operator');
const review = await operation.review();
console.log(review.native, review.nativeWorkspace);
```

Preparation reads the original private manifest and configuration. It validates
their existing bindings without loading the operator-key file or signer. Request
bodies and tickets are retained using the ordinary Node SDK path and original
native checks. The workspace evidence directory stays beside its policy and
ledger; the response destination remains in this Node application's operation.

The explicit workspace takes precedence over a Buyer constructor's default
operator profile. `operatorProfile` is not a `fromWorkspace` option. Supply
`responseFile`, `requestTimeoutMs` or `body` through the existing import options
when the request requires them; original review validates their limits.

## Adopt a separately authored request

To use an original generated client request or an explicitly selected next page,
pass its ordinary native configuration:

```js
const page = await buyer.fromWorkspace('/srv/private/operator', {
  configuration: '/srv/private/next-page.json',
  responseFile: {
    maxBytes: 1048576,
    timeoutMs: 30000,
    expectedContentType: 'application/json',
  },
  requestTimeoutMs: 90000,
});
console.log(await page.review());
```

`configuration` may also be a bounded JSON object. The original native workspace
helper composes it over the workspace configuration, then uses the same binding
checks as the durable inbox. Explicit operator, signer, evidence, payer or
transport changes must still match. The scheme, network, asset, recipient and
payment flow must match; the requested atomic ceiling must fit both the current
workspace and generated signer limits. A different wallet request remains an
explicit reviewed operation subject to the original service policy and ledger.

The authored intent is preserved. An optional `intentId` changes it only when the
caller explicitly selects a new identity during preparation. A duplicate
application intent is refused; it is never renamed to avoid a previous attempt.
No new page is selected or executed automatically.

## Execute once, then reopen the same result

```js
const review = await operation.review();
// Explicit operator action; requires the original controlling terminal.
const result = await operation.execute({ review });
console.log(result.native, result.record.runtimeError);
```

Before publishing this operation's permanent attempt, the original bridge
validates the current workspace, original ticket fingerprint, signer
prerequisites and controlling terminal. The SDK checks that the reviewed input
and workspace did not change during that preparation. Missing local setup leaves
this application's operation unattempted. Resolve the actual setup and review
the same operation again.

After an attempt is recorded, normal original terminal consent, native signing,
SF36 policy/reservation and SF31/SF82 execution apply. Only the three workspace
operator keys enter the native approval component. The manifest's selected
evidence RPC remains attached to its native execution options. Cancellation and
timeouts remain the existing subprocess and native execution behavior.

```js
// A new process using the SAME stateDirectory and exact intent.
const saved = buyer.operation(operation.intentId);
console.log(await saved.inspect());
const result = await saved.recover();
if (result === null) {
  console.log('Original result is not recorded; no automatic retry.');
} else {
  console.log(result.native, result.record.runtimeError);
}
```

Recovery reads the saved input/result and does not reopen the signer or require
the operator workspace to be mounted. Keep both original directories when
moving or recovering a customer installation. A successful native result and a
later saved-data interpretation failure are separate facts. Use the result's
original verified-file methods to read its returned bytes.

## Original inbox and accounting

Instead of direct execution, assign the prepared operation to an existing inbox:

```js
const inbox = buyer.inbox('/srv/private/buyer-inbox');
await inbox.enqueue(operation);
const inboxReview = await inbox.review(operation.intentId);
// Separate explicit action; the inbox owns this operation after delegation.
await inbox.execute(operation.intentId, {
  review: inboxReview,
  workspaceDirectory: '/srv/private/operator',
});
```

Delegation records the original nonreplaceable Node attempt marker. Direct
`operation.execute` then points back to that inbox; it cannot create a second
purchase. Use the existing inbox `recover`, `response`, `finalize` and
`exportReport` APIs with that original workspace. These keep the original
ledger, finality and output identities. Do not enqueue an already executed
direct operation.

Use `buyer.workspaceRecovery()` for the existing single-operator encrypted
backup and authenticated original-root restore, including this application and
any selected inbox. Its [recovery guide](RECOVERY.md) and maintained
`examples/recover_workspace.mjs` remain the implementations. The separate
runbook acquisitions API owns its multi-request workflow.
